content.text: Agent journey: with --format json, an error is printed as human text followed by the JSON on stderr. The contract (stderr ends with JSON) holds but agents must strip the prose. Worktree name wp-json-only-errors, trail #357. Find where errors are rendered for each format (the Report trait in crates/callisto-model/src/report.rs and the CLI error path) and choose the renderer once from the requested format so --format json writes only the JSON error object to stderr, while the default human format is unchanged. Test at the real binary boundary for one usage error, one config error and one release error: stderr parses as a single JSON document. Update docs/stability.md if it describes the stderr shape. Patch changeset written for people scripting Callisto. Rules (from the lead session close-gap-for-alpha): Read AGENTS.md first and follow its invariant ladder: a type or private constructor first, then exhaustive match, then an existing lint, then one test at the real boundary; delete per-call-site checks the new type makes redundant and migrate every sibling call site in the same PR. No new traits, async, journals or frameworks; no new error codes, JSON keys or flags without asking the lead first. Work in a named worktree off fresh origin/main (EnterWorktree name=<given>). Write the failing test first. Gate by exit code: just pre-push, just lint, just doc-check, just test, just ci; cargo mutants --in-place --in-diff on the Rust diff with zero missed or argued equivalents in the PR body; never commit mutants.out* (restore mutants.out.old from HEAD only if tracked). Run one fresh Opus reviewer subagent on the diff and apply what holds up. Changeset via `cargo run -p callisto-cli -- add --package cargo/callisto-cli:<bump> --summary "..."` only for user-visible changes, written for users. Signed commits, no session trailer. Right before pushing, merge the latest origin/main (no rebase, no force-push) and re-run the gates if it moved. Push with git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/<branch>, confirm with git ls-remote, link to the given Entire trail and open with entire trail ci-pr. If Entire raises findings, fix the ones that cause a wrong result, broken recovery, a security issue or a check that cannot fail; report the rest to the lead. Resolve a finding only after the fix is on the remote. When done, send the lead (close-gap-for-alpha) one report: PR number, sha, gates run, and anything not verified. CARGO_BUILD_JOBS is cores/5; never run two cargo builds in one worktree.

The brief's premise doesn't hold on current main, so I stopped without changing anything. No code changes, no commit, no PR, and no gates were run. The worktree `wp-json-only-errors` has a clean tree, but I couldn't sync it to the latest origin/main: the sandbox blocked `git fetch` and my `--ff-only` merge had no effect. It sits on `61d5dddc5`, which may not be the newest main.

**Handler errors are already JSON-only.** `crates/callisto-cli/src/main.rs:40` picks the renderer once from `--format`. With `--format json` it writes only `format_error_json(..)` to stderr, and the default human path is unchanged. I confirmed it with the real binary on a config error (E111, bad TOML) and a release error: both print a single JSON document. `crates/callisto-cli/tests/error_envelope_tests.rs` already asserts `serde_json::from_str(&stderr)` over the whole of stderr for status, version, add, pre, snapshot, init, matrix, compose-pr-body and every release and release-pr subcommand. That includes the "outside a repository" case, where the git tool's own message is suppressed. `docs/stability.md` lists stderr only as unstable text and says nothing about its shape, so it needs no edit.

**The real gap is clap parse errors.** `callisto --format json add --bogus` prints clap's human usage text and no JSON, because `Cli::parse()` exits before `format` is known. That is a different bug from the one briefed (prose followed by JSON). Fixing it means `Cli::try_parse`, spotting `--format json` in the raw args, and emitting an envelope. That needs an error code for a usage failure, and the rules say to ask you before adding one.

**Decision for you:** should I add a usage-error code, or reuse an existing one, for clap parse errors under `--format json`? If you say go, I'll write the failing binary-boundary test first, then the fix and a patch changeset.

I also deleted the tracked `callisto.toml` while cleaning up a stray repro file, then restored it with `git restore`, so the tree is clean.

9	| The eight commands (`add`, `status`, `version`, `pre`, `snapshot`, `init`, `release`, `completions`) and their flags | A flag keeps its meaning; a new flag never changes what the command did without it. |
10	| `--dry-run` | Accepted by every command, before or after the command name. Commands that write write nothing under it; on read-only commands it does nothing; where it cannot apply (for example `release plan`) it is a usage error. |
11	| Exit codes | `0` success, `1` failure, `2` usage error: a bad or missing argument or flag, including values the command validates after parsing; the same value read from `callisto.toml`, a changeset or another file is a failure, not a usage error. |
12	| `--format json` reports | Every report carries `schemaVersion`. Within a version a field is not removed, renamed or retyped; fields may be added. A shape change bumps the version. `release inspect` prints the intent, manifest or receipt unchanged: its own `schemaVersion`, no `command` or `dryRun`. `schema` prints JSON Schema documents, not reports. |
13	| `callisto.toml` | A key keeps its meaning. Unknown keys are an error, so a new key arrives in a minor release and never changes an existing file's behavior. |
14	| Changesets | The `.changeset/*.md` format and `pre.json` stay compatible with `@changesets/cli` 2.x and 3.x. `pre.json` is read in either shape and written back in the shape read: 2.x (`mode`, `tag`, `initialVersions`, `changesets`) or 3.x (`mode`, `tag`, with applied notes in `.changeset/pre/`). A cycle `callisto pre enter` starts uses the 2.x shape. The bare package name is the key unless another ecosystem has a package of that name, in which case the key is `ecosystem/name`. |
15	| Error codes | A code keeps naming the same condition and is never reused. New codes may appear. |
16	| Tag names | `{name}@{version}` by default, `ecosystem/name@{version}` once another ecosystem has a package of that name. Pin a name with `tag-template` if a stable tag matters to your tooling. |
17	| The GitHub Actions | The inputs of `callisto-action` and `setup-callisto`. Only the inputs and outputs documented as supported are promised; those marked Internal are not. The floating `v1` tag moves only on stable releases; pin a commit for a fixed version. |

They are hidden from `--help` and work only with the same Callisto version that generated them: the intent, decision, receipt and run envelope carry versions, and a reader rejects any other. Keep the action and the binary on one version, and regenerate with `callisto init` after an upgrade.
